text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz termed the present state of the banking and financial sector a multi-dimensional problem that cannot be solved without reducing mark-up (interest) rates.
- The National Bank of Pakistan and Dubai Islamic Bank have offered a credit of $50 million to Pakistan to import fuel oil.
- A five-member delegation from the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) met President Farooq Leghari to discuss the Karachi situation and the MQM accord with the ruling Pakistan Muslim League.

- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said she would resist the government's decision to terminate the power and port projects of Consolidated Electric Power Asia at Keti Bunder, saying it was criminal discrimination against Sindh province.
- The government has decided in principle to disband the Federal Investigation Agency and create a new police force to investigate white-collar crime.
- Eight people were gunned down in Karachi on Wednesday.
- Nearly two dozen textile exporters may lose orders worth 338 million rupees as the state-run Export Promotion Bureau has withheld the quota of one category of garment since January.
- Pakistan raised the minimum support price for different varieties of tobacco for 1997/98 (July-June) by 10 percent.
- Lahore High Court has admitted for regular hearing a petition by former military spymaster Hamid Gul against the arrest and extradition of Aimal Kansi to the United States.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the government would hold a population census by the end of this year.
- Pakistan will not seek leniency for the Pakistanis arrested in Saudi Arabia on charges of drug smuggling.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan said Pakistan had handed over 12 Chinese students, studying in religious institutions in Gilgit, to Chinese authorities.
